items.title: Democrats lead generic congressional ballot by 8-9 points, three weeks out
items.summary: RealClearPolling's generic ballot average has Democrats at 50.2% vs 41.9% for Republicans (+8.3); Silver Bulletin's average shows Democrats up 8.9 points (9.6 among likely voters), a cycle high with Democrats breaking 50% for the first time. Models give Democrats an 81-99% chance of retaking the House.

items.title: Senate battlegrounds: Democrats narrowly ahead in six tipping-point states
items.summary: Silver Bulletin's polling averages show Democrats leading in Maine (D+2.6), Texas (D+3.4), Ohio (D+3.7), Iowa (D+1.5), Michigan (D+3.3) and Alaska (D+3.4); even Kansas shows the Democrat ahead by 1.2. In Texas, Democrat James Talarico leads the Trump-backed Republican, campaigning on Trump going 'too far' on immigration. Models put Democratic Senate control at 55-64%.

items.title: GOP in 'triage mode' as Trump's approval sinks; one House Republican: 'Trump is dragging the party down'
items.summary: With three weeks to go, Republicans are diverting resources to defend once-safe seats amid voter anger over the Iran war and cost of living. Trump's net approval sits near -22, an all-time-low-adjacent reading. Despite a massive cash advantage via MAGA Inc., GOP spending has failed to shift the landscape. Trump, who called the midterms a referendum on his presidency, is pushing G7 diesel reserve releases to lower gas prices before Nov 3.

items.title: NewsNation-DDHQ poll: Democrats lead generic ballot 49-42, three weeks out
items.summary: A NewsNation/Decision Desk HQ poll conducted by TrueDot.ai, released Oct 13, finds Democrats leading Republicans 49% to 42% on the generic congressional ballot, with 8% undecided. Democrats also led 46-40 on which party has done more to earn voters' support.

items.title: Rasmussen: Democrats lead generic ballot 49-44, advantage widened 2 points in a week
items.summary: Rasmussen Reports' Oct 12 survey of likely voters has Democrats at 49% vs 44% for Republicans on the generic ballot, up from 47-44 last week — an 8-point swing against the GOP since before the 2024 elections. Independents favor Republicans 45-40; women back Democrats by 12 points while men prefer Republicans by 5.

items.title: DDHQ: Democrats have 76% chance of winning House; Trump favorability at 38/60
items.summary: Decision Desk HQ estimates Democrats have a 76% chance of taking the House. Its Oct 13 poll found Trump at 38% favorable vs 60% unfavorable; inflation (28%) and jobs/economy (20%) top voter concerns, immigration at 12%. 'You're basically out of time for much to change,' said DDHQ chief elections analyst Geoffrey Skelley.

items.title: Texas Senate: Talarico's lead over Paxton shrinks to 4 points (48-44) ahead of early voting
items.summary: A ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll released Oct 13 shows Democrat James Talarico leading Republican Ken Paxton 48% to 44%, down from a 6-point lead in September. Talarico leads independents 60-30; Paxton holds rural Texas by 18 points. No Democrat has won a Texas Senate seat since 1988. Early voting starts Oct 19.

items.title: Quantus poll: Paxton 47.2%, Talarico 46.7% — Texas Senate effectively tied
items.summary: A Quantus Insights survey of 839 likely voters puts Republican Ken Paxton at 47.2% and Democrat James Talarico at 46.7%, inside the margin of error. Paxton led voters 65+ by 17 points and held a 5-point suburban edge; Talarico led among independents, women, younger, Black, Hispanic and urban voters. RealClearPolling's average still has Talarico up 48.1-45.1.

items.event_time_ist: Rally announced Oct 13; rally Oct 19, Wichita
items.title: Trump to rally in Wichita Oct 19 for Sen. Roger Marshall as Kansas race becomes a toss-up
items.summary: The RNC announced Oct 13 that Trump will hold a midterm rally in Wichita on Oct 19 for Republican Sen. Roger Marshall, who faces Democrat Adam Hamilton in a race several pollsters now rate a toss-up. 'We can't win this without his voters,' Marshall said. Trump has been blitzing red states — Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas — and heads to North Carolina after Wichita.

items.title: Trump rallies in Ohio for Sen. Jon Husted amid competitive race against Sherrod Brown
items.summary: Trump held a midterm rally in Youngstown, Ohio on Oct 12 for Republican Sen. Jon Husted, who faces Democrat Sherrod Brown; he had campaigned in Vandalia on Oct 3 for Husted and GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. The RealClearPolling average has Brown leading Husted 47.4-44.3.

items.title: Cook Political Report moves 18 House races toward Democrats; Dems need just 20% of toss-ups
items.summary: Cook's Oct 9 ratings shift moved 18 races toward Democrats — nine GOP incumbents (Miller-Meeks, Nunn, Fitzpatrick, Perry, Huizenga, Wittman, Hill, Spartz and others), five Democratic incumbents, and four open seats. Cook's most likely outcome: Democrats gain 9-19 seats (224-234 total) and need only 20% of the 21 toss-ups for a majority. The NRCC dismissed it: 'House races are won in the districts, one by one.'

items.title: Prediction markets: Democrats 91% for House, 64% for Senate; sweep the leading scenario
items.summary: As of Oct 13, Polymarket priced Democrats at 91% to win the House and 64% to take the Senate; Kalshi's balance-of-power market also lists a Democratic sweep as the leading outcome. Polymarket's individual Senate markets favor Democrats in Texas, Maine, Michigan, Alaska and Ohio, while Republicans are favored in Iowa (Ashley Hinson). Market prices reflect trading, not polling.

items.event_time_ist: Data as of 7 AM ET, Oct 13
items.title: Michigan: mail ballot requests up 20% vs 2022; 440,677 ballots already returned
items.summary: Michigan officials said 2,083,240 voters had requested mail ballots — up over 20% from the same point in 2022 — and 440,677 had returned them (6% of active registered voters), slightly above 2022's pace. Michigan's gubernatorial race (Democrat Jocelyn Benson vs Republican Rep. John James) is among the key contests.

items.title: New Mexico: 21,022 ballots cast in first week of early voting; Democrats lead 12,526 to 5,504
items.summary: New Mexico's Secretary of State reported 21,022 ballots cast through Oct 8 in the first week of early voting (began Oct 6). Democrats cast 12,526 early ballots vs 5,504 Republicans; 2,868 unaffiliated voters also voted. Expanded early voting runs Oct 17-31.

items.title: Texas governor: Democrat Gina Hinojosa edges Gov. Greg Abbott 48-47 in YouGov poll
items.summary: A YouGov poll of 3,625 likely voters found Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa leading Republican Gov. Greg Abbott 48% to 47%, inside the 3-point margin of error. Both Democrats lead among women, Hispanic voters and voters 18-44; Republicans hold non-college and white voters. Early voting starts Oct 19.

items.event_time_ist: Poll published Oct 13, 2026; annual Governance poll conducted Sept 1-17, 2026
items.summary: Gallup's annual Governance poll finds the Democratic Party viewed favorably by 43% of Americans vs 35% for Republicans — an 8-point gap, above the 5-point long-run average. Democrats lead 44-33 on handling the nation's most important problem (a reversal from GOP +11 in 2022) and 51-37 on keeping the country prosperous, their largest edge since 2007. On protecting the U.S. from foreign threats, Democrats lead 46-42 — only the third time since 2002 the GOP has not led there. 59% call GOP views 'too extreme' vs 43% for Democrats. Independents drive the shift: 40% view Dems favorably vs 27% GOP; 50% of independents say Dems would keep the country prosperous vs 32% GOP. Gallup notes a majority still views the Democratic Party unfavorably overall.
items.title: Gallup: Democrats now hold the advantage on party image and the economy

items.event_time_ist: Ratings released Oct 13, 2026 (~12:54 PM IST, Oct 13)
items.title: MS NOW shifts Kansas Senate to 'lean Republican,' Minnesota to 'lean Democratic' in new ratings
items.summary: With three weeks to Election Day, MS NOW moved two formerly secure Senate seats into competitive territory: Kansas (Likely R -> Lean R) and Minnesota (Likely D -> Lean D). In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton is neck-and-neck with incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall - polls show them tied or Hamilton occasionally ahead in a state Trump carried by 16 points in 2024. The Senate Leadership Fund has reserved $8.2M+ in Kansas ads while pulling back from North Carolina, and VP JD Vance visited Kansas last month. RCP's polling average has the Kansas race a tie. Only MS NOW's own reporting plus republishers were found, so this is single-sourced.

items.title: Silver Bulletin asks whether recent Republican gerrymanders have become 'dummymanders'
items.summary: In its Oct 13 FLIPR forecast refresh, Silver Bulletin said the model has held steady for two weeks: Democrats remain strong House favorites and lead the polling averages of all six likeliest Senate tipping-point states (ME D+2.6, TX D+3.4, OH D+3.7, IA D+1.5, MI D+3.3, AK D+3.4) - with even Kansas at Dem +1.2. The same day, Silver Bulletin published a new post examining whether recent Republican gerrymanders have become 'dummymanders' - redrawn maps that backfire on the party that drew them. No second outlet has covered the post yet, so this is single-sourced.

items.event_time_ist: Lawsuit filed last week; reported Oct 13, 2026 (~6:10 AM IST, Oct 13)
items.title: Voting groups sue Texas over ~600,000 backlogged voter-registration applications
items.summary: The League of Women Voters of Texas and MOVE Texas Civic Fund sued the Texas Secretary of State and the Department of Public Safety in Bexar County last week over a backlog of nearly 600,000 unprocessed online voter-registration applications, seeking a permanent injunction to fix processing before Nov. 3. The groups say the backlog violates a 2021 settlement guaranteeing voters can register when renewing a driver's license; DPS blamed a third-party vendor software glitch and says it fixed the issue Sept. 13. Texas early voting begins Oct 19, and the Senate race (Talarico vs. Paxton) is among the tightest in the country. The filing itself is single-sourced to Democracy Docket (wire/AP only covered the underlying Sept 23 backlog story).

items.event_time_ist: early morning ET, Oct 12, 2026 (approx. 3:30–5:30 PM IST)
items.summary: Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a judicially authorized search warrant at Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington, D.C. home early Monday, carrying out boxes of evidence; the DOJ confirmed it is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation. Per NY Post sources, the years-long probe — involving whistleblowers — centers on alleged false statements in the Somalia-born congresswoman's immigration paperwork, possibly tied to her late father's citizenship application; no charges have been filed. Omar called it 'an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,' vowing she 'will not be silenced.' House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called the raid 'deeply disturbing'; Rep. Rashida Tlaib called it 'what a fascist police state does.' President Trump said he had 'nothing' to do with ordering it: 'I think she's a terrible person, but that's really up to the DOJ.'
items.title: DHS agents raid Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. home in immigration-fraud probe

items.summary: After the first days of early voting in Ohio, Democrats are showing unexpected strength in the state's most Republican counties, per Ohio Secretary of State data and Catalist analysis. In counties that voted for Trump by 20+ points in 2024, Republicans' 30-point lead in early voter shares has shrunk to 5 points; in the three most pro-Trump counties, the ballot-return partisan breakdown has shifted nearly 11 points toward Democrats vs. this point in 2024. The overall early electorate is ~27 points more Democratic than at the same point in 2024. Turnout pace: Harris counties at 74% of their 2024 pace, Trump counties at 67%. Separately, Signal Ohio reports early in-person voting is surging statewide while mail voting collapses: 20,030 early in-person ballots on day one across 56 counties vs. 8,647 four years ago (Cuyahoga County 1,908 vs. 547); mail voting is at just 25% of its 2024 pace, with Franklin County mail requests down to ~70,000 from 90,000+ in 2018/2022. A CNN poll also found Sherrod Brown leading Jon Husted by 6 points in the Ohio Senate race.
items.title: CNN: Democrats overperforming in early voting in Ohio's most Trump-friendly counties

items.event_time_ist: 2:49 PM EDT, Oct 13, 2026 (12:19 AM IST, Oct 14)
items.summary: Monroe County, Indiana (Bloomington) logged 2,686 early ballots in the first five days — more than 2% of registered voters — higher than any midterm since 2006 except 2018's record (3,933 in the same window), per the county's live early-voting dashboard. Indiana polls opened 28 days before Election Day. Indiana Public Media cites the Iran war, rising oil prices and Trump's domestic agenda as drivers; the state's restrictive voting hours and mail-ballot limits may still depress overall turnout.
items.title: Monroe County, Indiana: early voting turnout beats every midterm since 2006 except 2018

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026 — debate 7:00–8:00 PM ET (4:30–5:30 AM IST, Oct 14)
items.title: NY governor: Hochul and Blakeman face off in the race's only debate
items.summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) and Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman (R) met Tuesday night at NY1's Chelsea Studio for the only scheduled debate of the New York governor's race, airing on NY1/Spectrum News statewide. Clashes centered on affordability, Trump (mentioned by Hochul over a dozen times), and immigration — Blakeman hit Hochul over sanctuary policies days after an ICE shooting in the Bronx, and over her 2024 'misspoke' remark about Black Bronx kids not knowing computers; Blakeman tied her to NYC mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani. The debate lands with polls split: Marist has Hochul +11, Emerson +12, while a new Pollfinity survey has it 47-44. Debates rarely move NY statewide races, but Blakeman's campaign needs a viral moment amid a cash crunch.

items.title: NY governor poll: Pollfinity has Hochul 47, Blakeman 44 — outlier vs double-digit leads
items.summary: A new Pollfinity survey (499 likely voters, fielded Oct 8–12, MOE ~4.4) finds Gov. Kathy Hochul leading Bruce Blakeman just 47-44, with 6% undecided and 3% for others; with leaners it's 48-44. It sharply bucks the race's other recent polls: Emerson/PIX 11 (Oct 8) had Hochul +12 (52-40) and Marist had her +11 (53-42). Caveat: Pollfinity was founded in 2026 by California Libertarian Lars Mapstead and has no track record; the Post notes Blakeman is gaining vs Pollfinity's own June read (Hochul 50-40). Hochul's job approval sits at just 43% in the poll. Watch the Siena/Emerson next rounds for whether the tightening is real or house-effect noise.

items.title: Texas governor: ReconMR/Siena flips race back — Abbott 48, Hinojosa 47
items.summary: A new ReconMR/Siena poll (617 likely voters, MOE 4.4) has Gov. Greg Abbott (R) edging Democrat Gina Hinojosa 48-47 — a reversal from September's ReconMR read that had Hinojosa +4, and from the Oct 6 YouGov poll (Hinojosa +1) already in this feed. Abbott's job approval is 48-51; Hinojosa leads independents 57-34. Her campaign pushed back with an internal GBAO poll (800 LV) showing Hinojosa 47-45, cited on MSNBC's Maddow. RCP's Texas governor average sits at Abbott +1.7. Early voting starts Oct 19 — one of the most competitive Texas governor races in decades is now a coin flip.

items.event_time_ist: published Oct 13, 2026 (morning ET; missed by earlier checks, newly added)
items.title: Fox News Power Rankings: Democrats set to take the House, Senate 'stays in play'
items.summary: Fox News' weekly Power Rankings moved ~20 House races leftward this week: Democrats now hold an advantage in at least 219 seats vs Republicans' 198, with 18 toss-ups. On a 'good night' for Democrats the forecast sees them at ~237 seats (+22 from now); a GOP sweep of the toss-ups would leave Republicans at 216 — two short of a majority. Drivers: the Dem generic-ballot lead pushing red-leaning districts (KY-06, TX-15) left, Iowa and Pennsylvania statewide strength, GOP resources being pulled from races like NY-19, and what Fox flags as GOP trouble with rural voters. A 'great night' Democratic ceiling: 249. Note: forecaster's own release, published Oct 13 morning; no independent second outlet found.

items.event_time_ist: released Oct 13, 2026 (Manhattan Institute poll fielded Oct 9)
items.title: California governor: Becerra leads Hilton 55-38 in Manhattan Institute poll
items.summary: Democrat Xavier Becerra maintains a 17-point lead over Republican Steve Hilton in a Manhattan Institute poll of likely California voters fielded Oct 9: Becerra 55%, Hilton 38%, 7% undecided. Pushing leaners only shaves the margin to 57-39 — 'the electorate appears firmly settled behind the Democratic nominee.' Becerra holds 93% of Democrats, leads independents 48-39, women 59-33, and voters under 35 65-30. The lead matches other recent polls (Becerra +10 to +20+ in September surveys). Note: Manhattan Institute is a conservative-leaning think tank; its release is carried here by a single outlet so far.

A ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll released Tuesday, Oct. 13, finds James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 48%-44% in the Texas Senate race, a narrowing from 49%-43% in September. Independents favor Talarico 60-30; Talarico leads in Austin (72-21) and San Antonio/South Texas (56-38), is narrowly ahead in Dallas-Fort Worth and effectively tied in Houston, while Paxton leads rural Texas by 18 points. Talarico favorability is 48/43 (was 50/39), Paxton's 40/55. A separate University of Houston poll has Talarico leading in Harris County by nearly double the margin Rep. Collin Allred managed there in 2024.
items.title: Texas Senate: new ReconMR/Siena poll has Talarico 48, Paxton 44 — lead narrows from 6 points

items.event_time_ist: Published Oct 12, 2026; early voting begins Oct 19
items.summary: Dallas County elections administrator Paul Adams says just under 180,000 registered voters remain on the county's 'suspense' list — meaning their address needs confirmation — down from more than 200,000 a week ago after campaigns urged voters to check their registrations. More than 20,000 mail-in ballots have been mailed. Voters in suspense status can still cast a ballot after completing a statement of residence at the polls. In-person early voting in Dallas County begins Monday, Oct. 19.
items.title: Dallas County: ~180,000 voters on 'suspense' list ahead of Oct. 19 early voting start

items.summary: AdImpact data shows Republican campaigns, committees and aligned groups have outspent their Democratic counterparts by about $400 million so far this cycle. For the closing stretch, Republicans have $682 million in ads reserved from now through Election Day versus $491 million for Democrats. Senate Majority PAC communications director Lauren French conceded: 'We are being outspent by the Republicans. That's just a fact.' The gap is most acute in battlegrounds — Republicans are on track to outspend Democrats more than 8-to-1 on the Texas Senate race, per ad-tracking analysis.
items.title: GOP outspending Democrats by ~$400M on ads; Democrats privately sounding alarm

items.summary: Announced Oct 13: Trump will hold a 'Midterm Rally' Saturday Oct 17 at Truist Arena in Highland Heights, Kentucky (doors 10:30 AM, remarks ~2 PM) — home to the open McConnell Senate seat and KY-4; confirmed by the Enquirer plus Kentucky Lantern coverage. RNC also detailed the Wichita, KS rally Monday Oct 19 for Sen. Roger Marshall (remarks 6 PM), with Trump heading to North Carolina next on Wednesday Oct 21 (KRPS, single-sourced). Georgia's Dalton rally this Friday Oct 16 (announced Oct 12, third GA stop this year) was never in this feed — folded in. Third straight red-state weekend swing aimed at juicing base turnout three weeks out.
items.title: Trump adds Kentucky and North Carolina to his midterm rally blitz; Wichita stop detailed

items.event_time_ist: released Tue, Oct 13, 2026 (published ~2:30 AM IST, Oct 14); fielded Oct 8-11, 2026
items.title: Rhode Island governor's race tightens: WPRI/Emerson poll has Foulkes 44, Block 35 — lead cut from 24 to 9 points
items.summary: Democrat Helena Foulkes remains the clear front-runner in Rhode Island's governor race, but independent Ken Block has closed to a 9-point gap (44% to 35%), per a WPRI-TV/Emerson College poll of 800 likely voters fielded Oct 8-11, 2026 (MoE ±3.5). In August, Foulkes led a hypothetical matchup 45-21. Republican Aaron Guckian is at 10%, with 9% undecided. Block is outpolling the GOP nominee, leads among men (47-35) and unaffiliated voters (46%) — RI's largest bloc — but trails badly among Harris voters (72% for Foulkes). The lieutenant governor's race is a statistical tie: Sabina Matos (D) 44, John Loughlin (R) 45. Televised gubernatorial debate Oct 20; RI early voting starts Oct 14.

items.event_time_ist: released Tue, Oct 13, 2026 (reported 11:10 PM IST, Oct 13)
items.title: North Carolina Senate: Cooper +14 in new WRAL/SurveyUSA poll (54-40) — his strongest result yet
items.summary: Former Gov. Roy Cooper (D) leads former RNC chair Michael Whatley (R) 54% to 40% in a WRAL/WSOC poll conducted by SurveyUSA, released Oct 13 — Cooper's strongest showing, exceeding the margin of error. A separate Trafalgar Group poll (Oct 12) independently had Cooper ahead 48.8-40.9. The open seat (Sen. Thom Tillis retiring) is critical to Senate control: SLF cancelled $6.5M in NC ad reservations, Trump says he's 'worried' about Whatley, and Tillis endorsed Whatley while warning him against campaigning with Trump. NC early voting begins this week.

items.title: GOP pollster John McLaughlin disputes D+8 polls, says his firm's generic ballot has Democrats only +5
items.summary: Republican pollster John McLaughlin told Newsmax's 'Wake Up America' (aired Oct 12) that McLaughlin & Associates has Republicans trailing just 5 points on the generic congressional ballot, versus the ~8-point Democratic lead in the DDHQ average. He called the Economist/YouGov poll 'ridiculous' for oversampling Democrats, and claimed a re-framed question — free-market Republican vs big-government socialist Democrat — flips the result to Republicans 45-41. Urged the GOP to 'go on offense' on taxes, energy and government size with three weeks left. Single-sourced: only Newsmax has carried his firm's numbers so far.
